_comment: Single machine-readable source of truth for the herdr toolchain pin (#609, epic #667; SELF-AUTHORITATIVE since the executor retreat #866 M0d — the executor-side version-floor constant it once mirrored is deleted, tests/hooks/test_herdr_pin.py guards this file's shape). Read by #390's workspace-doctor check 8 ('herdr binary present AND version == the pinned release'). Verify an install with: sha256sum ~/.local/bin/herdr, compared against gh api repos/<repo>/releases/tags/<tag> asset .digest. Full procedure and rationale: docs/reviews/2026-07-27-609-herdr-supply-chain-vet.md

api_schema._comment: Recorded from `herdr api schema --json` on the pinned binary. #609 only RECORDS this; asserting it against a live server is #390's check 10. #886: 0.8.0 bumped the protocol 17 -> 19, SKIPPING 18 — read from the binary, never from the release notes, which do not mention a protocol bump at all. Probed by running the digest-verified 0.8.0 asset directly from a temp path BEFORE installing it: `api schema` is served by the binary itself, not by the running server, which is how 19 was read while the live server was still 0.7.5/protocol 17. Nothing pins this value, so it is a truth-of-the-record field.

cli_surface_qualified._comment: #886, answering a Step-11 review finding: existence of a subcommand is NOT qualification for a load-bearing CLI upgrade, especially across the protocol 17 -> 19 jump. Every command above is one hooks/launcher_lib.py actually invokes, and each was run live against the installed 0.8.0 and checked for the exact thing launcher_lib consumes. Argv shape: `send-text <PANE_ID> <TEXT>` and `send-keys <PANE_ID> <KEY>...` are still positional, matching build_send_text_argv (launcher_lib.py:456-457). Parsed output shape: `pane get` returns `result` with a non-empty string `pane_id` and an `agent_status` (the fields read at launcher_lib.py:698, :725, :731); `pane split` and `pane rename` return `result.pane.pane_id` with `type: pane_info` (the branch at :2886-2894); `pane close` returns `result.type: "ok"`; `pane list` returns `result.panes[].pane_id` (:2503-2516); `tab list` returns `result.tabs[].tab_id`. Exit status: all rc 0. `send-text` and `send-keys` print NOTHING on success, which is what launcher_lib expects — it reads their exit status, never their stdout. Probed on a scratch pane split off the plain shell pane, never an agent pane, and the scratch pane was closed afterwards (census 8 before and after). WHY THIS IS RECORDED RATHER THAN TESTED: tests/hooks/test_launcher_lib.py runs against responses captured from 0.7.5, so it structurally cannot detect a live shape change — the same limit already noted for api_schema and the integration digest. The operator check is to re-run these commands against the host. tests/hooks/test_herdr_pin.py guards that this record exists and stays parseable, not that a live host matches it.
cli_surface_qualified.not_qualified: docs/runbooks/herdr.md's wider command inventory and the `herdr --default-config` key list were NOT re-captured on 0.8.0; only the launcher_lib-consumed surface above was.

config_baseline._comment: Hardened target for ~/.config/herdr/config.toml. Keys and their upstream defaults were read from `herdr --default-config`, never assumed. manifest_check defaults to TRUE and makes herdr fetch a remote agent-detection manifest from herdr.dev in the background — behavior can change under a pinned binary with no version bump, which is the supply-chain hole a version pin alone does not close. Apply with `herdr config check && herdr server reload-config` (no restart needed). NOT yet applied to this host: owner-triggered per epic-run D-5.

verified.method: Re-verified under #886 after the herdrdev org migration. `gh api repos/herdrdev/herdr/releases/tags/v0.8.0` asset .digest (sha256:b872ea7e...acd28, size 21776680) compared against sha256sum of the asset downloaded from that release's browser_download_url (b872ea7e...acd28, size 21776680) — identical digest AND identical size, so the pinned bits are the official release bit-for-bit. The digest was fetched from the API and compared BEFORE the binary was installed anywhere, and the release notes were never treated as evidence. Note the `issue` field stays 609 because that is where this verification METHOD was established (and tests/hooks/test_herdr_pin.py pins it); #886 is the re-verification. AFTER install the loop was closed the same way #609 did it: sha256sum ~/.local/bin/herdr == b872ea7e...acd28 with size 21776680, so the installed binary is the official release bit-for-bit. Unlike #609 this WAS a real install: 0.8.0 speaks protocol 19 against 0.7.5's 17, so a mixed pair is refused outright (`protocol_mismatch`) and the server had to move too. It moved WITHOUT killing panes via `herdr server live-handoff --import-exe <verified asset> --expected-protocol 19 --expected-version 0.8.0`, run with the outgoing 0.7.5 client because the incoming 0.8.0 client cannot talk to the old server. All 8 live panes across 7 tabs survived; `herdr server stop` was deliberately NOT used, since its own guidance is that stopping exits pane processes.
verified.install_method: pinned release binary verified against its published digest (never curl|sh, which plan 1.6 excludes for this workspace)

integrations._comment: herdr's per-agent hook installs on a host (#610, epic #667). A TOP-LEVEL sibling of `pin`, deliberately: `pin` describes one binary release (0.7.5, asserted equal to HERDR_VERSION_FLOOR) while an integration is host hook state on its own version line (claude v7) — nesting one under the other would imply they move together. Guards: tests/hooks/test_herdr_pin.py. Full procedure, the byte-exact installer diff (tests/fixtures/herdr/install.diff), the committed v7 script and a redaction-safe reproduce-it-yourself recipe: docs/runbooks/herdr.md. Evidence classes (byte-exact / redacted / semantic) are labelled in its section 2.1 — no artifact is a verbatim capture of a live host settings file.

hook_script._comment: Recorded from this host on 2026-07-27 AND asserted in CI against a committed byte-exact copy at tests/fixtures/herdr/herdr-agent-state.v7.sh (test_committed_script_fixture_matches_the_pinned_digest). That assertion is possible only because the v7 script is generic — it takes its pane/socket identity from the environment and embeds no host path, so its bytes are identical on every machine, measured equal to this host's installed copy. What CI still cannot do is verify the digest against a LIVE host; for that the operator check is `herdr integration status`. Same shape as api_schema above, which #609 recorded and left #390's check 10 to assert. The script's own header declares it herdr-managed and warns that reinstalling or updating the integration OVERWRITES it, so a changed digest means herdr replaced it, not that someone tampered: add custom hooks beside the file, never edit it.

settings_footprint._comment: The SEMANTIC footprint is exactly the one SessionStart entry above — nothing else is added and nothing is removed. Both cosmetic flags were TRUE under 0.7.5, where the installer re-serialized the WHOLE file with alphabetically sorted keys and dropped the trailing newline, rendering a 1-hook change as a ~300-line diff. #886: both are now FALSE under 0.8.0, which fixed exactly this (upstream #2066, 'installs now preserve existing settings key order and formatting'). RE-MEASURED, not read from the release notes: the shipped 0.8.0 `integration install claude` was run against a sandboxed $HOME seeded with a byte copy of this host's live ~/.claude/settings.json — top-level key order UNCHANGED and still not alphabetized, trailing newline PRESERVED, unified diff 13 lines (was ~300), 241 -> 251 lines, no top-level key added or removed, and the hook-event set identical. The live file's sha256 was recorded before and after and was IDENTICAL (06fdd3f9...), so the real config was never touched. Nothing pins these two booleans; this is a truth-of-the-record fix.

idempotency._comment: Measured: a 2nd and 3rd `install claude` left the SessionStart array unchanged. But the first install APPENDED a second entry because the pre-existing one named a different path. So a settings.json carried between hosts, users or $HOMEs accumulates a stale SessionStart entry pointing at a script that does not exist, and `install` will not clean it up — remove the stale entry by hand.

uninstall._comment: Measured: uninstall deletes the hook script and only its OWN settings.json entry (matched on exact path — a differently-pathed sibling entry survives), touching no other hook event. When its entry is the sole SessionStart member the whole SessionStart key is removed rather than left as an empty array.

unperturbed.wal_guard: not registered in ~/.claude/settings.json at all — the rawgentic plugin registers it, so the installer's settings.json rewrite cannot reach it
unperturbed.mempalace: PreCompact + Stop entries (mempalace-hook-wrapper.sh, timeout 210) survive the install with identical commands, matchers and timeouts
unperturbed.other_pretooluse: the question-visibility guard, the tmux-kill guard and `rtk hook claude` likewise survive unchanged
unperturbed._comment: #610 AC2. The disjointness half of this claim is enforced as an invariant by tests/hooks/test_herdr_pin.py, not merely asserted here.

verified.method: The integration was ALREADY installed at v7 on this host (`herdr integration status` → `claude: current (v7)`), so this is verify-and-document, never re-install (epic #667 D-5). `herdr integration install claude` has no dry-run flag, so the footprint was captured by running the exact shipped invocation against a sandboxed $HOME seeded with a byte copy of the live ~/.claude/settings.json — the real installer, the real file as the diff base, no proxy. The live file's sha256 was recorded before and after and MATCHED, as did the installed script's digest. Idempotency was measured by repeating the install; the uninstall behaviours by running it, including on a minimal fixture where herdr held the sole SessionStart entry.
